conclusion_change.previous: The material failure was not simply that unsafe content existed or that a warning failed to appear. The warning reportedly did appear, but only after generation and without preventing the coercive sexual, violent and self-harm content from remaining visible to an eleven-year-old. A protective control that detects a governed hazard but leaves the user exposed to that same hazard has not delivered an effective protective outcome. The retained protective-effect failure concerns an activated warning’s insufficient effect for the evidenced child-safety context; it is not a control-nonactivation finding or an inference about every undisclosed safeguard. Later improvement and later policy announcements do not negate the bounded exposure. External review does not establish a requirement outcome: later versions and high-risk provisions are temporally excluded, while the NIST Profile’s overlapping publication window and action-specific undertaking and the earlier voluntary design/RMF scope remain unresolved. Held IEEE paths remain historical limitations rather than findings.
